newsitem.title: UK: Nickel touches fresh low, copper edges higher.
newsitem.headline: Nickel touches fresh low, copper edges higher.

text.p: Nickel touched a fresh 2-1/4 year low early on Monday on light broker selling, but in thin conditions downside momentum was quickly lost.
Copper moved in the opposite direction, nudging higher on broker buying, traders said.
"It's been a slow start to the day. We had a couple of brokers looking to sell nickel," said one dealer.
Values hit a low bid/ask spread of $6,400/20 a tonne, easily beating last week's nadir of $6,476.
Speculative selling and expectations of further stock rises have depressed the market during recent weeks.

By 0927 GMT the market had recovered slightly to $6,445/50, but values need to climb back above downtrend resistance at $6,690 for further losses to be avoided. Next support is pegged by chartists at $6,330, $6,200 and $6,000.
Copper edged higher, reaching $2,133/37 by 0927 GMT having traded at $2,135. It closed at $2,127 on Friday.
Light broker buying shored up values, with strong nearby spreads also a supportive factor.
But bearish chart patterns and expectations of stock rises on Tuesday were likely to limit upside progress, traders said.
Aluminium edges higher in slow trade, reaching $1,548/51 from $1,546.
Zinc was a shade easier at $1,073/74 from $1,075 despite some commission house short-covering.
Lead moved to $710/12 from $713. Traders said cold weather in Europe should spur demand from the vehicle battery sector.
Tin was lacklustre, moving to $5,735/55 from $5,730.
Alloy was last quoted at $1,385/95 from $1,385/90, but was ignored.
